arms.diagnostic_note: The control negative confirms the mechanism: undirected Steiner uses min(forward, reverse) edge costs, producing a cheaper-looking tree that becomes more expensive when traversed in the actual directed routing direction. The $11.36 per-config savings on inter-cloud configs comes from the directed DP selecting edges where the src→dst direction is genuinely cheap.

discrepancy_analysis: All predictions confirmed. The directed Steiner arborescence (Dreyfus-Wagner exact DP) scores 0.1594, beating undirected Steiner (0.1539) by 3.6% and baseline Dijkstra (0.0955) by 67%. The improvement is localized to inter-cloud configs (inter_agz, inter_gaz2) where cross-provider edge cost asymmetry is highest (up to 7.3x ratio). Intra-provider configs show no improvement because within-provider edges have near-symmetric costs. This confirms the causal mechanism: asymmetric edge costs in the directed graph create a gap between the undirected Steiner optimum and the directed Steiner optimum.
